# Manufacturing Business Glossary

This glossary defines the core business concepts and terminology used in the manufacturing supply chain domain. It covers product structures, materials management, production workflows, and quality assurance processes.

## Warehouse

A Warehouse represents a physical storage location where materials, components, and finished goods are stored. Warehouses have defined capacity limits, geographic location information, and are managed by designated managers. Warehouses serve as nodes in the supply chain network where inventory is held, shipments are received, and products are staged for production or distribution.

**Key Attributes:**
- Unique warehouse identifier
- Warehouse name and location
- Address, city, and ... [TRUNCATED]

## QualityControl

Quality Control (QC) represents inspection and testing activities performed on materials, in-process production, or finished goods. QC records track the type of inspection (incoming, in-process, final), inspection date, inspector, test results (pass, fail, conditional), defect counts, and notes. QC activities are associated with specific production batches and may reference technical specifications being tested.

tables_enriched.name: Product
tables_enriched.description: Stores information about products, including identifiers, names, type, hierarchical parent product relationships, base cost, lead time to fulfill, and whether the product is active.

tables_enriched.name: COMPONENT
tables_enriched.description: Stores data about components used in products, including identifiers, names, categories, units of measure, standard cost, and associated specifications.

tables_enriched.name: Bill of Materials
tables_enriched.description: Stores the bill of materials relationships, detailing which components (products) comprise a parent product, along with quantities and units of measure required at each BOM level.

tables_enriched.name: Supplier
tables_enriched.description: Stores information about suppliers including contact details, rating, and whether they are a preferred supplier.

tables_enriched.name: WAREHOUSE
tables_enriched.description: Stores information about each warehouse, including its identifying information, location, capacity, and the manager responsible for the facility.

tables_enriched.name: Inventory
tables_enriched.description: Stores inventory levels and restocking information for components and products across warehouses, including current on-hand quantity, reserved quantity, and the threshold to trigger reorders.

tables_enriched.name: WORK_ORDER
tables_enriched.description: Stores data about manufacturing or service work orders, including product details, quantities, status and scheduling, and the warehouse responsible for fulfillment.

tables_enriched.name: Shipment
tables_enriched.description: Stores records of shipments, including identifiers, involved warehouses, suppliers, and customers, as well as scheduled and actual arrival dates and current shipment status.

tables_enriched.name: Quality Control
tables_enriched.description: Stores records of quality control checks performed on production batches, including the date, type of check, inspector, results, and any defects or notes for traceability.

tables_enriched.name: Specification
tables_enriched.description: Stores specifications for products or processes, including identifiers, names, types, validity dates, and acceptable ranges for parameters.

tables_enriched.name: Batch
tables_enriched.description: Stores records of production batches, including which product was produced, quantities, dates, storage location, expiry, and quality control status.

tables_enriched.name: Component Supplier
tables_enriched.description: Stores the relationship between components and suppliers, including whether a supplier is preferred, typical lead time in days, and the unit price for each component-supplier pairing.
